title: Level 1 – Qualified Nurse
subtitle: Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice
intro: Welcome to GNPS Program 1 – Building Strong Foundations in Nursing Practice. Every successful nursing career begins with strong fundamentals. Before learning advanced clinical procedures or specialised nursing care, every nurse must develop a sound understanding of the core principles of nursing practice. This level is designed around the learning outcomes expected from national nursing education programs, such as those followed by the Country specific Nursing Council and similar nursing regulatory bodies across many countries. The focus is on developing the essential knowledge, skills, attitudes and professional behaviours required to provide safe, ethical and compassionate patient care. What You Will Learn Throughout this program you will strengthen your understanding of: • Professional roles and responsibilities of nurses • Basic patient care and comfort • Patient safety and infection prevention • Communication with patients and healthcare teams • Fundamental nursing procedures • Basic assessment and observation skills • Ethical and legal responsibilities • Documentation and reporting • Professional behaviour and accountability Why This Learning Matters The fundamentals of nursi

content.text: Nursing is more than a profession, it is a commitment to providing safe, compassionate, and ethical care. Every nurse, whether working in a hospital, clinic, or community setting, plays an essential role in improving the health and wellbeing of patients. Professional nursing practice begins with understanding your responsibilities and maintaining high standards of behaviour. Patients trust nurses not only for their clinical skills but also for their honesty, respect, and professionalism.
Learning outcomes

items: Explain the role of a professional nurse.
Recognise the importance of ethics and confidentiality.
Work within your scope of practice.

content.text: What is Professional Nursing? Professional nursing combines scientific knowledge, clinical skills, effective communication, and compassionate care. A professional nurse always places the patient's safety and wellbeing first.

Accountability Being accountable means accepting responsibility for your actions and decisions. If you administer medication, document care, or provide patient education, you are responsible for ensuring it is done safely and correctly.

Scope of Practice Every nurse must understand the limits of their professional role. When a situation is beyond your knowledge or authority, it is important to seek guidance from senior staff or the healthcare team.

Priya, a newly graduated nurse, is asked to insert a central venous catheter. She has observed the procedure but has never been trained to perform it independently. Instead of attempting the procedure, she informs her senior nurse and requests supervision. By recognising the limits of her competence, Priya protects her patient and demonstrates professional accountability.
Key learning points

items: Professional nursing is based on knowledge, ethics, and compassion.
Nurses are accountable for every action they perform.
Always practise within your scope of competence.
Never hesitate to ask for assistance when required.

content.text: Patient safety is the foundation of nursing practice. Every day, nurses make decisions that protect patients from harm and improve health outcomes. Even small actions—such as checking a patient's identity or ensuring the bed rails are secure—can prevent serious incidents.
Learning outcomes

items: Promote quality care in everyday practice.

content.text: Patient safety involves recognising hazards before they cause harm. Quality care means providing care that is:

During medication rounds, Ahmed notices that two patients have similar names. Before administering medication, he checks the identification wristband and confirms the patient's date of birth. Although this takes only a few seconds, it prevents a potentially serious medication error.
Key learning points

items: Small safety checks prevent major incidents.

content.text: Preventing infection is one of the most effective ways nurses protect patients and themselves. Many healthcare-associated infections can be avoided through consistent infection control practices.
Learning outcomes
Breaking the chain of infection begins with:

Before examining a patient, Maria performs hand hygiene. After completing the assessment and removing her gloves, she cleans her hands again before attending the next patient. This simple routine significantly reduces the risk of infection transmission.
Key learning points

items: PPE protects both patients and healthcare workers.
Follow standard precautions with every patient.

content.text: Excellent nursing care depends on effective communication and attention to patients' basic needs. Patients remember not only the treatment they received but also how they were treated.
Learning outcomes
Basic nursing care includes:
Good communication builds trust and improves patient outcomes.

Mr Sharma appears unusually quiet during the morning round. Rather than assuming everything is normal, the nurse sits beside him and asks how he is feeling. Mr Sharma explains that he has been experiencing increasing pain overnight but didn't want to trouble anyone. The nurse assesses the pain, informs the medical team, and provides appropriate care. Sometimes, listening carefully is the most important nursing intervention.
Key learning points

items: Small acts of kindness improve the patient experience.
Good communication is as important as good clinical skills.

By completing GNPS Program 1 – Level 1, you have developed the essential knowledge and practical skills that form the foundation of professional nursing practice. These fundamentals will support your growth as you progress to Level 2 – International Qualified Nurse, where you will apply these principles within international healthcare environments and evidence-based practice.
